title: Publish typed Rust, TypeScript, and Python clients
note: Per MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md, this task is implemented and its tests are written in this change, but manifest commands are not executed and status is not set to pass here. The orchestrator commits, runs the Wave 4 phase of the Book 3 final phased gate, and finalizes this evidence.

priorRelatedWork.note: The three typed clients this task publishes already exist on main from two prior, non-canonical commits that predate this task's dispatch and predate MBR-306: 979ef2b6 'feat(sdk): add typed Rust and TypeScript clients' (engine/crates/membrane-client, packages/typescript, tests/sdk/cross-language-compat.test.mjs, docs/sdk/README.md) and 5777c4a0 'feat(sdk): add typed Python client source contract' (packages/python, docs/sdk/python.md). Neither commit used the MBR-308 commit message or produced MBR-308 evidence, and both were authored before MBR-306 (13f9a63b) landed the real MBR-306 HTTP transport this task was asked to read and reconcile against. This task change does not re-author engine/crates/membrane-client/src/lib.rs, packages/typescript/index.mjs, or packages/python/src/membrane_client/client.py: their existing hand-written closed envelope validation (schemaVersion/errorVersion/operation exact match, closed top-level and result fields, closed per-operation error-code sets) was independently checked in this task against schemas/operations/membrane-context.v1.schema.json and schemas/operations/membrane-source-read.v1.schema.json and matches those schemas field-for-field and code-for-code; no drift was found requiring a source-of-truth-crate change within this task's allowlist.
priorRelatedWork.verifiedByThisTask: engine/crates/membrane-client/tests/compat.rs (new), the golden-fixture assertions added to tests/sdk/python_client_test.py (new PythonClientGoldenFixtureTest class), and the pre-existing tests/sdk/cross-language-compat.test.mjs together load and assert against the identical operations/operations/*.golden.json and operations-index.v1.golden.json fixture bytes for all three languages, which is the mechanical, non-review-based drift check this task's hard rules require.

implementation.gapClosed: Before this change, the Rust client (engine/crates/membrane-client) had source code but no `cargo test` target of its own: its behavior was only exercised indirectly by regex/substring assertions against its source text from tests/sdk/cross-language-compat.test.mjs. This change adds engine/crates/membrane-client/tests/compat.rs, a real Cargo integration test that loads the same operations/operations/*.golden.json and operations-index.v1.golden.json fixtures the TypeScript and Python suites use and exercises MembraneClient directly: golden success extraction, golden typed-and-retryable error mapping for both membrane_context and membrane_source_read, every operations-index error code round-tripping as a typed error, and fail-closed behavior for an out-of-index error code, a schemaVersion/operation mismatch, an unknown top-level field, and an unsupported operation. This is the deterministic Rust-side half of 'all SDKs pass the same compatibility test suite.'
implementation.pythonStrengthened: tests/sdk/python_client_test.py previously validated envelope handling only against hand-authored dict literals that mirrored, but were not read from, the canonical fixtures. This change adds PythonClientGoldenFixtureTest, which loads operations/operations/membrane-context.v1.golden.json, membrane-context.v1.error.golden.json, membrane-source-read.v1.golden.json, membrane-source-read.v1.error.golden.json, and operations-index.v1.golden.json directly (the exact files tests/sdk/cross-language-compat.test.mjs and the new Rust test read) so the Python suite is proven against identical fixture bytes, not an independently authored equivalent that could silently drift.
implementation.httpTransportDoc: docs/sdk/http-transport.md is new. MBR-308's dispatch explicitly directed reading engine/crates/membrane-runtime/src/mcp_http.rs and engine/crates/membrane-mcp/src/http_security.rs (MBR-306, landed as 13f9a63b) 'so the clients speak the transport that actually exists.' Those crates are membrane-runtime (RESERVED by a concurrent lane) and membrane-mcp (not in this task's allowlist), so this task cannot add a shipped HTTP transport implementation inside either SDK package without writing outside its allowlist or duplicating membrane_mcp::http_security's admission policy inside the SDKs, which the task description ('never duplicate policy logic in SDKs') and the existing SDK design (docs/sdk/README.md: 'Each client takes an injected transport; none opens a socket, retries, starts, stops, or discovers a daemon') both forbid. Instead this task documents, in the in-allowlist docs/sdk/ directory, the exact wire contract (POST /mcp, Host/Origin/Authorization/x-membrane-installation-id/x-membrane-session headers, the full closed denial-code enum from schemas/http-mcp-security.v1.schema.json) a caller needs to write a correct transport function, and states plainly, from reading engine/crates/membrane-mcp/src/jsonrpc.rs and tools.rs, that the shared McpServer::dispatch's tools/call branch is currently a stub ({"content":[..."native_tool_execution_unsupported"...],"isError":true}) for every tool call regardless of transport, so no SDK today can complete a live operation round trip over either stdio or HTTP tools/call; only golden fixtures and directly injected transports exercise the operation envelope contract right now. This is a factual statement grounded in the current source, not a claim of a working HTTP client shipped in the SDKs.
implementation.mechanicalTransportDriftCheck: tests/sdk/http-transport-contract.test.mjs reads engine/crates/membrane-runtime/src/mcp_http.rs's MCP_HTTP_PATH/INSTALLATION_HEADER/SESSION_HEADER string constants and schemas/http-mcp-security.v1.schema.json's denial enum at test time and asserts docs/sdk/http-transport.md still names every one of them, plus asserts engine/crates/membrane-client/tests/compat.rs still reads all five shared golden/index fixtures. This is the 'checked against the shared schema so drift is caught mechanically' requirement applied to the transport-contract documentation, without adding any dependency or touching a reserved/out-of-allowlist crate.

knownGap.description: tests/sdk/*.test.mjs (both the pre-existing cross-language-compat.test.mjs and the new http-transport-contract.test.mjs) are not invoked by the repository root package.json's "test" script, which is currently `node --test mcp/*.test.mjs scripts/*.test.mjs && pnpm run legal:verify`. Running `pnpm test` today does not execute either SDK compatibility test file. Fixing this requires editing /Volumes/D/claude/membrane/package.json, which is outside MBR-308's allowlist (engine/crates/membrane-client/**, packages/typescript/**, packages/python/**, schemas/**, tests/sdk/**, docs/sdk/**), so it is not changed by this task per the hard rule to stop and report a file outside the allowlist rather than write it.
knownGap.recommendation: A follow-up (in-allowlist for package.json, e.g. the Book 3 integration step or a dedicated task) should extend the root "test" script's node --test glob to include tests/sdk/*.test.mjs so the Wave 4 gate's `pnpm test` command actually exercises this task's compatibility suite. Until then, the suite is proven only by direct invocation: `node --test tests/sdk/cross-language-compat.test.mjs tests/sdk/http-transport-contract.test.mjs` and `cargo test --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml -p membrane-client` and `python3 tests/sdk/python_client_test.py`, all of which this task ran (Rust excepted, per the hard no-cargo rule) and recorded in commands.log.
